editorial:
Imagine being a teenager and suddenly feeling like your world is glitching. You follow a young Indigenous boy who is trying to navigate his life, but things get weird fast. He starts seeing things that aren't there and feels like he is slipping between different versions of reality. It feels like a mix of a family drama and a strange dream, where you aren't quite sure what is real and what is just in his head. The vibe is a bit heavy but has some funny moments that keep it from feeling too sad, making you really root for the kid as he tries to figure out why his life is falling apart.

The acting is the best part here because the lead feels like a real person, not a movie character. The way the story jumps around might confuse you at first, but it makes the reveal of the family secret feel much more powerful. If you like stories about family secrets and mental struggles, you will love this.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out the strange visions were caused by a deep family trauma and a secret about his heritage. The boy finally stops fighting the weird images and accepts the truth about his past. He has a heart-to-heart with his family, which helps him ground himself back in reality. The movie wraps up with him finding peace and feeling more connected to his roots, showing that honesty is the only way to heal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about family secrets and coming-of-age journeys.
